units: NZD per unit unless stated; net assets in millions
method: NAV-per-unit compounding with exit price-to-NAV multiple. NOT an FCF DCF.
valuation_philosophy: Booster Innovation Fund (BIF) is a listed venture-capital unit trust holding ~40 unlisted, early-stage NZ deep-tech companies. It has no revenue, no EBITDA, no capex and no free cash flow to shareholders in any operating-company sense -- its 'operating cash outflow' is capital deployment into new and follow-on investment rounds, funded mostly by fresh unit subscriptions rather than realised returns. A standard FCF DCF is therefore meaningless here and was rejected outright, exactly as this research folder handles AFI.NZ (LIC: NTA + exit discount), FIH.U (holdco: BVPS growth x exit P/B) and FRFHF (insurer: BVPS compounding x exit P/B). Instead this model compounds NAV PER UNIT forward from the manager's latest observable strike price, applies a scenario exit price-to-NAV multiple in year 5, and discounts the single terminal exit value back at a venture-appropriate cost of equity -- there are no interim cash distributions to discount, because BIF has paid unitholders nothing since a single $568k distribution in FY2022. The discount rate is built up to ~20% (versus a typical 9-11% cost of equity for a diversified operating business) because four structural risks stack on top of a plain NZ equity cost of capital: (1) 100% of NAV is Level 3 manager-marked with no external price test, and the manager's own performance fee depends on the mark it sets; (2) the fund has realised zero exits in over five years, so the entire compounding thesis is unproven in cash terms; (3) the listing is extremely illiquid (Yahoo shows a nominal $1.504-$1.508 range across the trailing year) with a tiny free float once Booster's own KiwiSaver/Super/ACNL holdings are excluded, so a holder cannot simply sell into a liquid market at the model's fair value; and (4) the underlying assets are seed/early/expansion-stage ventures where individual total loss is a normal outcome, not a tail risk -- the fund's own disclosure quietly drops liquidated holdings from its reported portfolio table. The most important and most adverse single data point in this whole analysis is that the manager's own most recent unit issue (3-Jul-2026, 255,337 units at $1.4759) priced BELOW the 31-March-2026 audited NAV of $1.5114 and below the 24-March-2026 mark of ~$1.534 -- i.e. the manager itself has marked NAV down since the annual report was signed. That is used as the current NAV base for this model rather than the higher audited figure, and it is treated as a genuine warning sign about the sustainability of NAV growth, not smoothed away. Because BIF trades via manager-struck application/redemption rather than an order book, it has always priced at ~1.0x NAV (currently 99.8% of audited NAV, 102.2% of the July strike) -- the complete absence of the 20-40% discount-to-NAV that would normally give a value investor a margin of safety in a listed VC vehicle is itself the central risk of buying at $1.508. This model's honest conclusion is that BIF is fully to over-valued at the current price under any defensible discount rate: even the base case, built on continuation of the fund's own historical 4.87% per-unit NAV CAGR plus a modest re-rate, produces a meaningful double-digit downside once discounted at a rate that reflects Level 3 marking, zero realisations, illiquidity and venture-stage risk. This is not a reverse-engineered bearish output -- it falls directly out of discounting a single, distant, uncertain terminal value at ~20% with no interim cash return to cushion the wait, and it mirrors the negative-weighted-IV conclusion this repo already published for AGL.NZ.

inputs.nav_current_basis_source: 3-Jul-2026 unit issue (255,337 units at $1.4759/unit, effective 1-Jul-2026) -- the manager's own most recent strike price, used in preference to the higher 31-Mar-2026 audited NAV of $1.5114 because it is more current and because it embeds a subsequent mark-down the annual report does not yet reflect
inputs.net_debt_treatment_note: Net debt is set to zero, not to (debt - cash) = -$0.326m net cash. Cash is already fully inside NAV per unit, so adding it again on top of a NAV-based valuation would double-count the same asset. Total debt is genuinely zero -- the fund carries no borrowings, only trivial tax/other payables.
inputs.ownership_structure: Booster KiwiSaver Scheme 55.7%, Booster SuperScheme 8.9%, related ACNL holdings additional -- genuine independent free float is well under 10%
inputs.sbc: not applicable -- BIF is a unit trust with no employees or equity compensation scheme; BIML (the manager) is remunerated via management/performance fees, not equity
inputs.interest_income: not applicable -- fund does not hold meaningful interest-bearing cash (1.3% of net assets); no adjustment made
inputs.fcf_dcf_note: Not applicable. No revenue, EBITDA, capex, working capital or FCF exists for this vehicle -- see valuation_philosophy. All standard FCF-DCF schema fields (WACC/Gordon terminal value, SBC adjustment, share dilution) are replaced by the NAV-compounding equivalents below.

historical_growth.net_assets_total_growth_warning: Net ASSET TOTAL grew at a 34.2% CAGR FY2022-FY2026, but this is almost entirely new unit issuance (units on issue grew 27.9% CAGR over the same period), not investment performance. The only per-unitholder-relevant growth measure is NAV PER UNIT, which compounded at just 4.87% p.a. over the same 4 years. Using the asset-total CAGR as a growth driver would overstate this fund's investment performance by roughly 7x.
historical_growth.eps_note: EPS/NI-per-unit is not a meaningful driver here -- FY2025's -$1.739m loss and swings driven by unrealised fair-value marks make a NI-based CAGR noise, not signal (a mechanical 3yr NI/unit CAGR is -52.7%, which is a Level-3-marking artefact, not an investment-performance conclusion)
historical_growth.equity_cagr_note: Shareholders' equity (=net assets) 3-4yr CAGR of 20-34% reflects capital raising, not investment performance, and should NOT be used as the growth driver for this ticker -- see net_assets_total_growth_warning above.
historical_growth.fcf_note: Not applicable -- no FCF concept exists for this vehicle.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: nav_per_unit_cagr_4yr_fy22_fy26 (the only per-unitholder-relevant growth measure available)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Net-asset-total CAGR (34.2%) diverges enormously from NAV-per-unit CAGR (4.9%) -- entirely explained by new unit issuance funding the difference, not by investment outperformance. Standard equity-CAGR growth-rate selection logic is inapplicable to a fund that issues new units continuously; NAV per unit is used instead of total equity/asset CAGR for this reason.
historical_growth.notes: The realised NAV-per-unit CAGR of 4.87% p.a. since inception (FY2022-FY2026) is the historical anchor for the base case. It embeds one very good year (FY2023: +11.4%), one good year (FY2024: +10.7%), one bad year (FY2025: -8.3%) and one moderate recovery (FY2026: +7.0%) -- i.e. it is already a blended, volatile realised track record over a full market cycle, not a smooth compounding trend.

wacc_rationale.methodology: Cost of equity built up from a NZ risk-free rate and equity risk premium, plus four additive structural premiums specific to BIF. A typical 9-11% operating-company cost of equity would be indefensible for a 100%-Level-3, zero-realisation, illiquid, early-stage-venture portfolio.

component_rationale.level3_manager_marked_no_price_test_prem: 100% of NAV is Level 3 (manager-marked, unlisted holdings) with no external market price test, and the manager's own performance fee is contractually tied to the NAV it sets -- an inherent conflict of interest (+2.0-3.0% range used at 2.5%)
component_rationale.zero_realisations_untested_exit_thesis_p: Only $568k has ever been distributed (FY2022 only, against ~$20m+ deployed); the entire venture exit thesis underlying reported NAV gains is unproven in cash terms across more than five years (+1.5-2.5% range used at 2.0%)
component_rationale.extreme_illiquidity_tiny_free_float_prem: 52-week trading range of $1.504-$1.508 is nominal, not a functioning secondary market; Booster's own KiwiSaver (55.7%), SuperScheme (8.9%) and related ACNL holdings leave well under 10% genuine independent free float, so a holder needing liquidity outside the manager's own application/redemption window may find none (+2.0-3.0% range used at 2.5%)
component_rationale.early_stage_venture_total_loss_risk_prem: Underlying holdings are seed/early/expansion-stage NZ deep-tech companies where individual total loss is a normal outcome, not a tail event; the fund's own disclosure drops liquidated companies from its reported portfolio table entirely, meaning the visible 40-holding portfolio understates historical failure rates (+2.0-3.0% range used at 2.5%)

base.nav_growth_rationale: Compounds near the fund's own realised 4.87% NAV-per-unit CAGR since inception, drifting modestly higher (5-6%) as the disclosed portfolio matures (60% of holdings now 'Expansion' stage vs a more seed-heavy historical mix) and NZ venture follow-on capital remains buoyant (record Icehouse/Bridgewest fund closes, +$100m Elevate top-up in Budget 2025). Starts from a lower 4.0% in Y1 reflecting the adverse July-2026 mark-down signal.
base.exit_rationale: A modest normalisation toward the ~0.6-0.9x discount typical of listed VC/PE trusts, reflecting that BIF's current at-NAV pricing (a function of manager-struck application/redemption, not an order book) is not obviously sustainable if the listing ever develops genuine secondary trading or if scrutiny of Level 3 marking increases.

bull.nav_growth_rationale: One or more portfolio companies achieve a genuine cash exit or a large uplift financing round -- venture power-law dynamics. Alimetry (US$18m Series A2, FDA clearances, CPT III reimbursement code) and Allegro Energy are the most plausible candidates; a single scaled outcome could re-rate the whole $24.7m NAV given the fund's small size.
bull.exit_rationale: A proven realised exit converts the manager's marks from theoretical to demonstrated, justifying pricing back at par NAV -- consistent with where BIF already trades today.

bear.nav_growth_rationale: Follow-on rounds come at down-valuations, several early-stage holdings fail outright (consistent with the disclosed practice of dropping liquidated companies from the portfolio table), and the manager's marks prove to have been optimistic -- a repeat and extension of the FY2025 -8.3% experience. The July-2026 below-NAV unit issue is read here as the leading edge of this scenario.
bear.exit_rationale: The listing re-rates to a conventional 0.70-0.80x VC-trust discount once BIF's captive related-party buying support (Booster's own KiwiSaver/Super schemes) softens or once independent unitholders demand a margin of safety against unverified Level 3 marks.

projections.distributions_note: No interim distributions are projected in any scenario -- BIF has paid unitholders nothing since a single $568k FY2022 distribution, and there is no PDS commitment to future payouts. All projected return is therefore terminal (year-5 exit) and illiquid; there is no dividend/coupon cushion in the interim years, which is a substantive fact about this investment, not a modelling simplification.
projections.unit_count_note: Per-unit basis throughout. Ongoing unit issuance at (or near) NAV is value-neutral to existing unitholders and is NOT modelled as future dilution or accretion -- issuing new units at NAV neither creates nor destroys per-unit value for existing holders, so the year-5 unit count is irrelevant to this per-unit valuation.

base.implied_exit_multiple: n/a -- P/NAV valuation, not an earnings or FCF multiple

valuation.note: terminal_pct_of_value is 100% in every scenario by construction -- there are no interim cash flows to discount, only the single year-5 exit value. This is the direct consequence of BIF never having distributed to unitholders (bar the one-off FY2022 $568k payment); the entire investment case is a single, distant, all-or-nothing terminal realisation.

entry_price.methodology: With no interim cash flows, the usual entry-price formula (PV of interim FCF at 15% + PV of terminal value at 15%, less net debt) collapses to a single term: entry price = year-5 base-case exit value / 1.15^5. This is a substantive fact about BIF, not a modelling shortcut -- the fund distributes nothing, so 100% of the return an entry-price buyer requires must come from the terminal exit alone.

base.pv_interim_note: Zero because BIF has never paid a recurring distribution and none is projected.

sanity_check.description: Standard P/E, EV/EBITDA and P/Sales sanity anchors are meaningless for a fund with no revenue or earnings in the operating-company sense; the only valid sanity metric for a listed venture/investment trust is price-to-NAV.
sanity_check.historical_pnav_context: BIF has traded at essentially 1.0x NAV throughout its listed history (99.8-102.2% currently) because units transact via manager-struck application/redemption rather than a genuine secondary order book. This is itself anomalous versus the ~0.6-0.9x price-to-NAV discount typically demanded by the market for listed VC/PE trusts globally, where investors price in illiquidity, Level 3 valuation uncertainty and manager conflicts of interest. BIF's at-NAV pricing is therefore the central risk in this analysis, not a sign of fair value -- a re-rate to a normal trust discount would be a 10-30% price fall with ZERO change in the underlying portfolio's fair value, purely a re-pricing of the wrapper.
sanity_check.trip_reason: Base-case intrinsic value ($0.69) is 54% below the current price ($1.508), far outside the +/-30% tolerance band. This is flagged, not silently passed, because it reflects the deliberate combination of (a) using the manager's own most recent below-NAV strike price as the NAV base, (b) a venture-appropriate ~20% cost of equity, and (c) a fund with zero interim distributions to cushion the multi-year discounting period. All three inputs are independently well-supported by the disclosed facts (see valuation_philosophy and wacc_rationale) -- the trip is the intended, honest output of this model, not an error.
sanity_check.note: The check is reported as failed/tripped deliberately: it signals that $1.508 prices BIF as if it were a proven, liquid, professionally-verified compounder, when the evidence (zero realisations in five years, a below-NAV manager strike three months after the FY2026 balance date, and a captive rather than independent buyer base) supports a materially more conservative valuation.

sensitivity.methodology: IV = (NAV_current_basis x (1+g)^5 x exit_P/NAV) / (1 + 20% CoE)^5, varying the flat 5-year NAV growth rate g and the year-5 exit price-to-NAV multiple -- the two dominant levers in this model.

cost_of_equity_sensitivity.description: Secondary sensitivity: base-case IV (6% terminal-year NAV growth trajectory, 0.90x exit) as cost of equity varies +/-3pp around the 20% central estimate.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Base case is weighted most heavily as the direct continuation of the fund's own realised NAV-per-unit track record. Bear is weighted above the usual quarter given the concrete adverse evidence already in hand (FY2025's -8.3% NAV year and the July-2026 below-NAV manager strike). Bull is weighted below the usual quarter because it requires a specific, as-yet-unrealised cash exit event that has not occurred once in the fund's five-year history.

verdict: At $1.508, BIF prices essentially at (in fact slightly above) the manager's own latest NAV strike of $1.4759, leaving no discount-to-NAV margin of safety of the kind normally demanded for an illiquid, Level-3-marked, zero-realisation venture vehicle; discounting the only plausible source of return -- a single, distant, uncertain year-5 exit at a ~20% venture-appropriate cost of equity -- produces a base-case intrinsic value of roughly $0.69 (-54%) and a probability-weighted intrinsic value of roughly $0.72 (-52%), so the current price is not attractive on this analysis.
